messages:
maria: Heads up — after the kernel selection update (v2.14) we started seeing 99th tail spikes on mixtral-moerouter around 18:04 UTC. Small prompts (~64 tokens) are worst.
kevin: which knob changed in v2.14? batching? kernel heuristics?
maria: main change was probabilistic top-k routing default (topk=8 probabilistic) and a new kernel path that defers some kv-copy work to async thread. Also RoPE scale tweak in the model profile (scale=1.02) rolled in for a few tenants.
nina: any sign it's routing rather than kernel? cache metrics?
maria: yes — eviction rate jumped from 4.2% -> 14.9% on router-expert-1 pools. KV cache hit for live traffic fell ~62% -> 41%. Latency correlates with eviction bursts.
perf-bot: [automated] perf delta: 99p latency +34%, p50 +6%, KV eviction +10.7pp. Flame graph and allocation diff: https://perf.redwood/reports/1976543210
ashley: can you reproduce locally with a synthetic replay? also try toggling deterministic topk.
maria: ran replay at qps 500 on canary cluster: reproduces. Changing router to deterministic topk (set router.topk_mode=deterministic) reduces 99p by ~18% immediately.
kevin: interesting — probabilistic topk seems to increase expert churn which evicts KV more. Could be interaction with async-kv-copy kernel path.
nina: agree. hypothesis: probabilistic routing increases expert fanout per request, raising concurrent KV writes. async-kv-copy defers work but still competes for L2/L3, causing eviction cascade.
ashley: steps to triage?
maria: 1) rollback probabilistic topk -> deterministic (temporary) 2) revert kernel async-kv-copy to sync path on canary 3) instrument per-expert active-set sizes + per-GPU memory pressure histograms 4) try increasing topk from 8->4 and gating by batch size.
kevin: I can push a hotfix to routing layer to add a soft cap: if batch_size < 16 then topk=4. Quick config change: runtimectl set mixtral.router.heuristics.small_batch_topk=4
deploy-bot: deploy started for mixtral-canary config at 1976544500
maria: after putting small_batch_topk=4 on canary, 99p dropped ~22% and eviction rate down to 6.3%. Performance looks much better.
ashley: did you try reverting async-kv-copy kernel too?
maria: tried revert on one canary shard — no further improvement beyond the topk cap. suggests routing change is dominant for these small prompts.
nina: what about RoPE scale? any model-quality regressions from rolling back that tweak?
maria: RoPE scale was a minor tweak for long-context stability; toggling it didn't affect eviction or latency. We kept it for now but will run evals.
kevin: long term we should add router-aware kernel selection: if routing fanout predicted > X then prefer sync-kv-copy path that groups writes (avoid many small async ops). Also consider routing temperature scheduling: more deterministic under low batch sizes.
ashley: agreed. Action items: KEVIN add router-aware kernel flag + perf test, MARIA roll canary change to prod with small_topk cap after 1h healthy, NINA add expert-level mem/active metrics and KV hit client-side logs, MATT (ops) monitor.
maria: I'll open a follow-up with config diff and perf graphs.
kevin: also add a short-term mitigation: if KV eviction rate > 10% then throttle probabilistic routing and force topk cap automatically.
maria: noted. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [automated] follow-up checklist created: https://perf.redwood/tasks/1976543210/checklist
ashley: leaving a note — this was a nice example of cross-layer regression: routing heuristic + kernel path interacting with cache pressure. worth a doc.
maria: will write a short postmortem and include kernel selection heuristics, routing knobs we touched, and suggested longer-term scheduler work (router-aware grouping, adaptive topk, better per-expert admission control).
